description: Second-order 1-bit sigma-delta modulator in the canonical CIFB topology with all loop coefficients equal to 1/2, so the whole noise-shaping loop is two shift-add integrators plus a sign test and no multiplier. a is the s12 input; c[1:0] picks how many oversampled sub-steps (1..4) the beat retires with that same input, c[31] clears both integrators first, and c[30:2] must be zero. result is the 1-bit DAC level as +/-2046, sign extended. aux[0] = the last sub-step bit, aux[3:1] = how many of this beat's sub-steps went high, aux[4] = an integrator clamped (the loop left the s12 +/-1.0 full-scale stable range), aux[5] = restart echo, aux[19:8] and aux[31:20] = the new x1 and x2 integrator states in s12. fault = any integrator clamped or malformed control.
hardware_advantage: One beat can retire up to four oversampled modulator steps through an unrolled shift-add loop, so a Class-D output bit stream at 1 MHz costs a quarter of the sample-rate budget in software; the loop needs no multiplier, no ROM and 32 bits of state, which is what makes 50 parallel modulators fit next to the rest of the audio path.
provenance: original source authored in this workspace; no third-party RTL imported
qualification: engineering candidate; not certified production or side-channel protection
